rationale: Hosea 12 names Jacob and Bethel: 'In the womb he grasped his brother’s heel, and in his vigor he wrestled with God ... he found Him at Bethel and spoke with Him there' (12:3-4, BSB). The prophet names the patriarch and the place, so the type is explicit_reference. It is graded strong, not explicit, following conn-gen25-twins-malachi1 and conn-gen19-lot-deuteronomy2 (a later text that names the persons but leaves which earlier scene is meant to the reader), because Genesis records two encounters at Bethel and readers differ on which Hosea means. Keil and the Pulpit Commentary on Hosea 12:4 say it is 35:9-15, not 28:11-19; Jamieson-Fausset-Brown cites both 28:11-19 and 35:1; Barnes' Notes says 'Both revelations ... are probably included'; the Cambridge Bible says either 'may have been current' in Hosea's circle. The Pulpit Commentary gives Hosea's order as its reason: the Bethel vision meant 'comes after that at Penuel', the wrestling of Genesis 32. The row's toRange covers 12:3-5 because 12:3 supplies the name Jacob that 12:4 continues.
